title: Checkout call-site audit scanner has a sticky test-scope flag: any column-0 cfg(test) line silently unaudits the rest of the file
wanted_capability: scripts/acceptance-checkout-callsites.sh should track test scope structurally instead of via a sticky flag. Today the scanner sets in_test=true on any column-0 "#[cfg(test)]" line and never resets it for the remainder of the file, so a bare test-gated item (e.g. an unindented "#[cfg(test)] use ..." import) placed before a real acquisition site makes the scanner classify every later call as test-only. The audited site then "no longer exists" per checkout_callsite_audit_is_complete even though the code and the TSV ledger are both correct, and the failure message points the author at editing the ledger, which is exactly the wrong fix. Wanted: brace-depth or item-scope aware test detection (or at minimum resetting the flag at the next top-level item), plus a failure message that distinguishes "site vanished from the scan" from "row is stale", so authors are not steered toward weakening the ledger.
missing_primitive: scope-aware cfg(test) detection in the checkout call-site scanner
fallback_used: Removed the stray column-0 cfg(test) import from src/server/producer_auth.rs and kept test-only imports inside the trailing cfg(test) mod tests block, matching the shape the scanner expects (feat/producer-grant-rotation, sha 7f12891d).
evidence: scripts/acceptance-checkout-callsites.sh: in_test set on any line starting '#[cfg(test)]' and never reset for the rest of the file
